title: AIA Rock 'n' Roll Manila 2026 Review: What the 2025 Night Race Was Like
seo_title: AIA Rock 'n' Roll Manila Review: Night Course, Weather, Cut-offs
meta_description: AIA Rock 'n' Roll Manila review: the 2025 midnight marathon's three laps from Rizal Park, 25-27°C and 90% humidity, a 7h30 limit, a 5:37 median and a 3:01:29 winning time.
dek: What running the Rock 'n' Roll series' Manila night race was like in 2025: the three-lap course through Intramuros and over Jones Bridge, a warm and humid night, the aid stations and cut-offs, how fast the field ran, and the race-week logistics.
verdict: Enter if you want a night marathon in central Manila with a generous limit and a recreational field. The 2025 marathon started at 12:01am at Kilometre Zero by Rizal Park and ran three laps of a loop through Intramuros, over Jones Bridge and round Anda Circle, with a 7 hour 30 limit. The median finisher took 5:37, and the winner 3:01:29. Starting at midnight keeps the sun off, but it does not make the race cool: it was 25-27°C all night with humidity around 90% and almost no wind. If you dislike laps or struggle in humid air, think twice. If you do enter, plan your own electrolytes, and expect water stations every kilometre or so on each lap.

sections.heading: The Course: Three Laps From Kilometre Zero
paragraphs: The 2025 race was on Saturday 29 November, a day earlier than first announced [10]. Every distance started at Kilometre Zero on Roxas Boulevard by Rizal Park: the marathon at 12:01am, the half marathon at 2am, the 10 km at 5am, the 5 km at 6am and a new 1 km kids' run at 6.45am. All of them finished on Katigbak Parkway, across from the Manila Hotel entrance [2]. Pre-race reports put the field at over 8,000 runners [5][13]; on race night the Daily Tribune said over 9,000, more than double the first edition four years earlier [6]. The results list 1,275 ranked marathon finishers, plus 11 marathon times without a place, along with 2,471 half-marathon and 2,114 10 km finishers [1].

The marathon is three laps. Runners collect a coloured lap band at Kilometre Zero after the first lap (km 14) and the second (km 28) [2]. The organiser's course page, now carrying the 2026 dates, describes the loop: south on Roxas Boulevard to a turnaround at Quirino Avenue (km 2), back north past Rizal Park and along Burgos Avenue to a turnaround at Orosa Street and Kalaw Avenue (km 5), over Jones Bridge to a turnaround just before Plaza Lorenzo Ruiz in Binondo (km 7), back over the bridge and through Intramuros by General Luna street, then along Bonifacio Drive to a turnaround at Anda Circle (km 13) and back to Kilometre Zero. After the third lap, runners turn at Anda Circle onto Katigbak Parkway to finish [3]. The page warns that some of its maps may still show the previous year's course [3].

The half marathon runs two laps of a similar loop, turning on Burgos Avenue just before the National Museum instead of crossing to Binondo, and the 10 km is one lap [3]. A Daily Tribune columnist who ran the 21 km described it as two loops from Kilometre Zero, through Intramuros and back along Roxas Boulevard, and found it repetitive [7]. Because the half starts at 2am and the 10 km at 5am on the same roads [2][3], marathoners share the loop with those fields on their later laps.

The organiser says the courses are measured by World Athletics and AIMS [3], and Philstar's preview described the route as AIMS-certified and on fully closed roads [5]. The guide lists 28 entertainment stations along the marathon course [2], and the Tribune's race-night report described live bands, DJs and themed stations along the route [6].

sections.heading: Night-Race Weather: Warm and Very Humid
paragraphs: Open-Meteo's historical model for the grid point over Rizal Park gives 25.6°C at midnight on race night, with 90% humidity and a dew point of 23.8°C. It barely changed until dawn: 25.0°C to 25.2°C from 2am to 6am, humidity 90-91%, and 25.6°C at 7am. Wind stayed under 4 km/h from midnight to 7am, cloud cover was mostly between 70% and 100%, and the only rain was 0.1 mm at 3am. The model's apparent temperature was 30-31°C all night [8].

Ninoy Aquino International Airport, about 9 km south-east of the start, recorded slightly warmer conditions: 27°C with a dew point of 25°C and 89% humidity at midnight, the same at every hourly report until 7am apart from 94% humidity at 6am, and a wind of 2-3 knots. By 8am, half an hour after the course closed, it was 29°C [9].

A midnight start keeps the sun off the marathon, but it does not bring cool air. With dew points of 23-25°C, sweat barely evaporates, and the temperature did not drop through the night. The Tribune columnist singled out the humidity when complaining that stations served lukewarm water with no ice [7].

sections.heading: Aid Stations and Cut-offs
paragraphs: The 2025 guide lists ten hydration stations on the marathon course, one every 1 to 1.25 km, each with Amlan water, portable toilets and a medical station. Ion+ electrolyte drink was at stations H1, H3, H5, H7 and H8, and GU gels only at H8 [2]. Ten stations at that spacing cover roughly one 14 km lap, so marathoners pass them on each of the three laps. The half-marathon guide lists nine stations per loop, with electrolyte at four and gels at one [2]. The runners' checklist tells runners to bring their own nutrition, and a head torch is optional [2].

The marathon time limit was 7 hours 30 minutes from the gun, with the finish closing at 7.30am, and the only intermediate cut-off listed was at km 28 at 4.59am [2]. That checkpoint works out to about 10:39 per km, almost exactly the pace of the full limit, so it is no tighter than the finish. The half marathon had 5 hours 30 minutes, with a cut-off at km 10.5 at 4.59am; the 10 km had 2 hours 30 and the 5 km 1 hour 30, and every distance had to finish by 7.30am [2].

The results suggest the limit was applied at the finish: the slowest marathon time listed is 7:30:06, and about one in ten ranked finishers took more than seven hours [1]. Finisher shirts went only to official marathon and half-marathon finishers [2].

sections.heading: How Fast the Field Is
paragraphs: The fastest ranked marathon times were 3:01:29 for men and 3:15:34 for women, and tenth place was 3:35:05 for men and 3:58:28 for women. Four faster times, from 2:40:33 to 2:50:19, appear in the results without an overall place [1]. In the half marathon the winners ran 1:14:45 and 1:33:18, with tenth place at 1:29:18 and 1:45:10; the 10 km winners ran 37:44 and 44:46 [1].

This is a recreational field. The median ranked marathon finisher took 5:37, and the slowest tenth of the field took longer than 6:58. Of the 1,275 ranked finishers, 7% broke four hours, 15% broke 4:30, 31% broke five hours and 62% broke six, and 22% were women [14]. In the half marathon the median was 2:42 and the slowest tenth took more than 3:36, with 11% under two hours and 38% under 2:30; 39% of half-marathon finishers were women. The median 10 km finisher took 1:27, 9% ran under an hour, and 49% of 10 km finishers were women [14]. A sub-four-hour marathon here puts you in the top 7%.

The marathon grew in 2025 and got slower. Ranked marathon finishers rose by 13%, from 1,127 in 2024 to 1,275, and the median slipped by eight minutes, from 5:29 to 5:37. The half marathon shrank by 6%, from 2,640 to 2,471 finishers, with its median unchanged at 2:42, and the 10 km grew by 8%, from 1,958 to 2,114, with a median about a minute slower [14][15].

sections.heading: Race Weekend Logistics
paragraphs: Race kits were handed out at the health and wellness expo in the Midtown Wing exhibit area of Robinsons Place Manila, on Pedro Gil in Malate, from Monday 24 to Thursday 27 November, 11am to 7pm; there was no collection on the Friday or on race day. Runners needed photo ID and the QR code from their NJUKO confirmation email, and anyone collecting for someone else needed ID, a letter of authorisation and the registration email, all printed [2].

On race night the gear-bag drop opened at 9pm on Friday at South Road Drive, across from the Rizal Park Hotel, and accepted only the bag issued with the kit; bags could be collected until 9am. Marathon check-in opened at 11pm, with assembly at the start at 11.30pm [2]. After the finish, runners went to the post-run area at Quirino Grandstand for finisher shirts, food and the festival, where four headline acts played between 4am and 7.30am [2]. The Tribune columnist found the post-race meal of canned tuna over rice a let-down [7].

The guide points runners to jeepneys, e-trikes, taxis and ride-hailing apps such as Grab, inDrive, JoyRide and Angkas [2]. In 2025 the marathon cost PHP 4,266, the half PHP 3,780, the 10 km PHP 2,970 and the 5 km PHP 2,322, including tax and processing fees [10]. Runners who entered two distances, a marathon or half plus a 10 km or 5 km, could earn an extra Remix Challenge medal [2].

sections.heading: Should You Enter the 2026 Race?
paragraphs: Yes, if you want a night marathon through Manila's old centre, with music along the course and a 7 hour 30 limit that few runners test: in 2025 half the marathon field finished after 5:37, but nine in ten were home by 6:58, more than half an hour before the course closed. A sub-five-hour marathon puts you in the top third.

Think twice if you dislike laps, because the marathon covers the same loop three times and shares it with the half-marathon field from 2am, or if you struggle in humid air: in 2025 it was 25-27°C with a dew point of 23-25°C all night. Carry your own electrolytes and gels, as the 2025 course had gels at only one station per lap.

The 2026 race, the fifth edition, is on 29 November [11][12], so the marathon starts at 12:01am on Sunday, late on Saturday night. The organiser's course page lists the same start times and time limits as in 2025 [3]. Its race-week page gives expo dates of 24 to 27 November, 11am to 7pm, a gear-bag drop from 9pm on Saturday 28 November and a 7.30am finish cut-off for all distances, but it names two different expo venues and says the 2026 runner guide is not yet available, so check the guide before you travel [4]. The 2026 theme is Filipino music, with medals designed with National Artist Ryan Cayabyab [12].

Nobody from this site ran the race. This review draws on the organiser's 2025 runner guide and course pages, the full results, modelled and airport weather records, Philippine news reports, and one runner's published column.

faqs.question: What time does the AIA Rock 'n' Roll Manila marathon start?
faqs.answer: At one minute past midnight. In 2025 the marathon started at 12:01am on Saturday 29 November at Kilometre Zero on Roxas Boulevard, followed by the half marathon at 2am, the 10 km at 5am and the 5 km at 6am. The organiser lists the same start times for 29 November 2026, a Sunday.

faqs.question: What are the cut-off times at Rock 'n' Roll Manila?
faqs.answer: Generous for a marathon. In 2025 the limit was 7 hours 30 minutes from the gun, with the finish closing at 7.30am and one intermediate cut-off at km 28 at 4.59am. The half marathon had 5 hours 30 minutes, the 10 km 2 hours 30, and every distance had to finish by 7.30am.

faqs.question: How hot is the Rock 'n' Roll Manila night race?
faqs.answer: Warm and humid, despite the midnight start. On race night in 2025 the modelled temperature over Rizal Park stayed at 25-26°C from midnight to 7am, with humidity of 90-91% and a dew point near 23.5°C. Manila airport, about 9 km away, recorded 27°C and a 25°C dew point all night, with almost no wind.

faqs.question: What is the Rock 'n' Roll Manila course like?
faqs.answer: Three laps of a loop of about 14 km for the marathon. From Kilometre Zero by Rizal Park it goes south on Roxas Boulevard, over Jones Bridge towards Binondo, through Intramuros and round Anda Circle, finishing on Katigbak Parkway by the Manila Hotel. The half marathon does two laps of a similar loop.

faqs.question: How fast is the field at Rock 'n' Roll Manila?
faqs.answer: Mostly recreational. In 2025 the median marathon finisher took 5:37, one in ten took longer than 6:58, and only 7% of the 1,275 ranked finishers broke four hours. The fastest ranked times were 3:01:29 for men and 3:15:34 for women. In the half marathon the median was 2:42, and 11% of finishers ran under two hours.

faqs.question: Where do you collect your race kit for Rock 'n' Roll Manila?
faqs.answer: At the race expo, before race weekend. In 2025 kits were handed out at Robinsons Place Manila in Malate from Monday to Thursday, 11am to 7pm, with none on the Friday or race day. Bring photo ID and your confirmation QR code. For 2026 the organiser gives expo dates of 24 to 27 November.

editorial_notes: Written 2026-11-06 about the previous edition (Saturday 29 November 2025, organised by Sunrise Events for the Rock 'n' Roll Running Series). Results are the full Sportstats lists. The marathon list has 1,286 runners with a finish time, but 11 of them, including the four fastest (2:40:33 to 2:50:19), carry no overall place, so the winning times, top-ten times, median and percentages use the 1,275 ranked finishers; 84 listed marathoners have no time. Winners are given by time, not name. Sportstats displays times rounded up to the second. Weather is from the Open-Meteo historical model for the Rizal Park grid point and from Manila airport METAR reports, about 9 km away, not a forecast. The course description comes from the organiser's course page, which now carries 2026 dates and warns that some maps may show the previous year's course; the three-lap layout matches the 2025 guide's lap bands at km 14 and km 28. The guide lists only 'Intermediate Cut off 2' (km 28) for the marathon; no first cut-off was found. The 2026 race-week page names two expo venues; neither is stated as fact here. Road-closure details for 2025 were reported by the Manila Bulletin, but the page could not be opened, so they are left out. The only first-hand runner account found is a Daily Tribune column by a half-marathon runner; no blogs, Reddit threads or vlogs from runners were found. No rating. Updated 2026-11-06 with Run SEA analysis of the 2025 and 2024 Sportstats results (ranked finishers only): 90th-percentile times, share of women, and change from 2024.
